questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (Only 2 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is incorrect: human gametes are haploid cells containing 23 chromosomes (half the somatic diploid count of 46). Statement 2 is correct: spermatogenesis produces hundreds of millions of microscopic motile spermatozoa, while oogenesis matures a single ovum per menstrual cycle. Statement 3 is correct: the vas deferens joins the ejaculatory duct at the urethra, forming a common conduit for semen and urine in males.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about work: 1. Pushing a rigid wall does no work on the wall, because the wall is not displaced. 2. If a force acts perpendicular to the displacement of an object, the work done by that force is zero. 3. Work has no direction; it is described by a number with a positive or negative sign. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (All of 1, 2 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: mechanical work W = F * s * cos(θ); without displacement (s = 0), work done is zero. Statement 2 is correct: when force is perpendicular to displacement (θ = 90°), cos(90°) = 0, so work is zero. Statement 3 is correct: work is a scalar quantity described completely by magnitude and algebraic sign (positive, negative, or zero).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How does the way cnidarians obtain food differ from that of poriferans?
options: Both use tentacles to catch prey
Both depend on water currents through pores
Poriferans use tentacles; cnidarians use water currents
Cnidarians use tentacles; poriferans use water currents
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (Cnidarians use tentacles; poriferans use water currents) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Cnidarians (e.g., Hydra, jellyfish) are predatory carnivores that capture prey using stinging tentacles equipped with cnidocytes. Poriferans (sponges) are sessile filter feeders that draw water through ostia via flagellated choanocyte currents.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In a healthy adult, about 180 litres of filtrate is formed in the kidneys daily, but only a litre or two of urine is excreted. This is because
options: Most of the filtrate is re-absorbed in the kidney tubules
Most of the filtrate is stored in the urinary bladder
Most of the filtrate is lost as sweat
The kidneys filter only a small volume of blood
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (Most of the filtrate is re-absorbed in the kidney tubules) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). The nephrons of adult kidneys filter approximately 180 litres of initial glomerular filtrate daily, but > 99% of filtered water, glucose, and essential electrolytes are selectively reabsorbed along the renal tubules back into peritubular capillaries, yielding only 1-2 litres of concentrated urine.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which cells in the phloem regulate the cellular functions of the sieve tube cells?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (Companion cells) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Sieve tube elements lose their nuclei and major organelles upon functional maturity; their metabolic and cytoplasmic transport activities are maintained by nucleated companion cells connected via plasmodesmata.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Magnesium ribbon in air (i) Oxide dissolves in water to form an alkali (b) Aluminium oxide (ii) Reacts with both acids and bases (c) Sodium oxide (iii) Burns with a dazzling white flame (d) Copper heated in air (iv) Gets a black coating of copper(II) oxide Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | ((a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iv)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Magnesium ribbon burns in atmospheric oxygen with an intense dazzling white flame to yield white MgO powder (a-iii). Aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and bases, acting as an amphoteric oxide (b-ii). Sodium oxide dissolves in water to form alkaline sodium hydroxide (c-i). Copper heated in air oxidizes to form a black surface coating of copper(II) oxide CuO (d-iv).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the human female reproductive system: 1. The ovaries make the eggs and also produce some hormones. 2. When a girl is born, her ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs. 3. After puberty, one egg is produced every month by one of the ovaries. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (All of 1, 2 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: ovaries produce ova and secrete estrogen and progesterone. Statement 2 is correct: at birth, a female infant's ovaries contain hundreds of thousands of primary oocytes arrested in meiotic prophase I. Statement 3 is correct: beginning at menarche, hormonal cycles prompt one mature ovum to be ovulated alternately each month.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, but its solution in water does. What is the reason?
options: Water gives electrons to the ions
Solid sodium chloride has no ions in it
The ions become free to move in the solution
Sodium chloride becomes a covalent compound
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (The ions become free to move in the solution) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). In solid sodium chloride, Na+ and Cl- ions are immobilized within a rigid crystalline lattice by strong electrostatic ionic bonds. When dissolved in polar water, hydration energy overcomes lattice energy, freeing mobile ions to conduct electric current.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A girl lowers a dumbbell by 40 cm while holding it with an upward force of 60 N. What is the work done by her force on the dumbbell?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (−24 J) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). The girl applies an upward force F = 60 N while the dumbbell moves downward by displacement s = 40 cm = 0.4 m. The angle θ between upward force and downward displacement is 180°. Work done W = F * s * cos(180°) = 60 N * 0.4 m * (-1) = -24 J.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Ribosome (i) Cell's post office (b) Golgi apparatus (ii) Powerhouse of the cell (c) Lysosome (iii) Site of protein synthesis (d) Mitochondrion (iv) Single-membrane sac of enzymes Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | ((a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptide proteins (a-iii). The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages macromolecules for cellular delivery or secretion (a-iii, b-i). Lysosomes are single-membrane acid hydrolase vesicles that digest cellular waste (c-iv). Mitochondria generate cellular ATP via aerobic oxidative phosphorylation (d-ii).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Bryophytes (i) Seeds enclosed in fruits (b) Pteridophytes (ii) Seeds exposed on cones (c) Gymnosperms (iii) Called plant amphibians (d) Angiosperms (iv) True roots, stems and leaves, no seeds Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | ((a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Bryophytes lack vascular tissue and require external water for flagellated sperm fertilization, earning them the title 'amphibians of the plant kingdom' (a-iii). Pteridophytes possess vascular bundles and differentiated roots/stems but reproduce via spores without seeds (b-iv). Gymnosperms bear naked ovules on cones without protective ovaries (c-ii). Angiosperms produce flowers and enclose seeds within fruits (d-i).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about cells: 1. Mature human red blood cells have no nucleus, which leaves more space for haemoglobin. 2. The genetic material of a prokaryotic cell lies inside a well-defined nucleus called the nucleoid. 3. Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (Only 1 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: mature mammalian erythrocytes shed nuclei and organelles to maximize cytoplasmic volume for oxygen-carrying hemoglobin. Statement 2 is incorrect: prokaryotic nucleoids lack any surrounding nuclear membrane or structural envelope. Statement 3 is correct: ribosomes are ubiquitous universal sites of protein synthesis.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about oxides and acids: 1. Metal oxides react with acids to give a salt and water, so they are called basic oxides. 2. Non-metallic oxides, such as carbon dioxide, are basic in nature. 3. Acids produce H⁺(aq) ions in solution, which are responsible for their acidic properties. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (Only 1 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: basic metal oxides react with acids to produce salt and water (neutralization). Statement 2 is incorrect: non-metal oxides (like CO2, SO2) dissolve in water to yield acids and are acidic in nature. Statement 3 is correct: Arrhenius acids dissociate in aqueous solutions to yield hydronium/hydrogen ions H+(aq).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Thomson's model spreads the positive charge evenly, so alpha particles fired at a thin gold foil should pass straight through or deflect only slightly. Which observation of the gold foil experiment contradicted this expectation?
options: Most alpha particles passed through undeflected
Alpha particles are nuclei of helium atoms
A few alpha particles bounced back
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (A few alpha particles bounced back) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). In Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment, Thomson's plum pudding model predicted all alpha particles would pass through undeflected. The startling observation that roughly 1 in 8,000 alpha particles rebounded through angles > 90° demonstrated that all positive charge and mass reside in a tiny, dense atomic nucleus.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the placenta: 1. It is a disc embedded in the uterine wall. 2. Its villi and the surrounding maternal blood spaces provide a large surface area for glucose and oxygen to pass from the mother to the embryo. 3. Waste substances produced by the embryo are transferred into the mother's blood through it. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (All of 1, 2 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: the placenta is a specialized discoid vascular organ implanted into the uterine endometrium. Statement 2 is correct: chorionic villi interdigitate with maternal blood pools, providing expansive surface area for diffusion of oxygen and nutrients. Statement 3 is correct: metabolic nitrogenous wastes and CO2 produced by the fetus diffuse across the placenta into maternal circulation.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Assertion (A): Desert plants can take up carbon dioxide at night. Reason (R): The steps of photosynthesis need not take place one after the other immediately.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R correctly explains A: desert plants (CAM plants) open stomata at night to absorb CO2 and fix it into malic acid, preventing daylight transpirational water loss; daytime solar energy then drives light reactions and Calvin cycle decarboxylation.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about reproduction in human females: 1. An egg that is not fertilised remains viable for about a day and then degenerates. 2. Ovulation is the shedding of the uterine lining along with some blood. 3. The implantation of the zygote in the uterus marks the beginning of pregnancy. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (Only 1 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: an unfertilized ovum survives approximately 24 hours in the fallopian tube before degenerating. Statement 2 is incorrect: ovulation is the release of a secondary oocyte from the Graafian follicle (menstruation is the shedding of the uterine lining). Statement 3 is correct: blastocyst implantation into the endometrium establishes gestation.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Assertion (A): In the spectrum of white light formed by a glass prism, red light bends the most. Reason (R): Different colours of light bend through different angles with respect to the incident ray as they pass through a prism.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (A is false but R is true) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Assertion (A) is false: in glass prism dispersion, red light has the longest wavelength and highest refractive velocity, so it deviates the least, while violet light deviates the most. Reason (R) is true: the refractive index of glass varies inversely with wavelength, causing different spectral colors to refract at distinct angles.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Autotrophs (producers) (i) Third trophic level (b) Herbivores (ii) Fourth trophic level (c) Small carnivores (iii) First trophic level (d) Larger carnivores (iv) Second trophic level Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | ((a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Autotrophic primary producers occupy the first trophic level (a-iii). Herbivores (primary consumers) occupy the second trophic level (b-iv). Small carnivores (secondary consumers) occupy the third trophic level (c-i). Top apex carnivores occupy the fourth trophic level (d-ii).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Isaac Newton placed a second identical prism in an inverted position behind the first and passed all the colours of the spectrum through it. The light emerging from the second prism wa
options: A beam of red light only
A band of only violet and red
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (A beam of white light) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Sir Isaac Newton demonstrated that sunlight dispersion into spectral colors is an intrinsic property of light: placing a second identical inverted prism recombined the separated spectral rays back into a singular beam of white light.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A train moving at 72 km/h applies its brakes and comes to rest in 20 s. What is its average acceleration?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (−1 m/s²) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Initial speed u = 72 km/h = 72 * (5 / 18) = 20 m/s. Final speed v = 0 m/s in time t = 20 s. Acceleration a = (v - u) / t = (0 - 20) / 20 = -1 m/s^2.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: On a position-time graph, a vehicle is at 20 m at t = 1 s (point A) and at 110 m at t = 4 s (point B). What is the magnitude of its average velocity between A and B, which is the slope of line AB?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (30 m/s) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). On a position-time graph, average velocity equals the slope of the secant line: v_avg = (x2 - x1) / (t2 - t1) = (110 m - 20 m) / (4 s - 1 s) = 90 m / 3 s = 30 m/s.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about plastids and vacuoles in plant cells: 1. Chromoplasts are colourless plastids that store starch. 2. Some leucoplasts in potato cells store starch. 3. The large central vacuole maintains pressure inside the cell, which keeps a plant cell firm. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (Only 2 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is incorrect: chromoplasts contain carotenoid pigments imparting yellow/orange/red colors; colourless storage plastids are leucoplasts. Statement 2 is correct: amyloplasts (a type of leucoplast) store starch granules in potato tubers. Statement 3 is correct: the tonoplast-enclosed central vacuole develops hydrostatic turgor pressure that keeps plant cells rigid.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why does a single-celled organism not need specific organs for taking in food and exchanging gases?
options: It needs no energy for its life processes
Its entire surface is in contact with the environment
It does not use oxygen to break down food
It has specialised tissues for uptake of food and oxygen
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (Its entire surface is in contact with the environment) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Unicellular organisms like Amoeba maintain a microscopic surface area-to-volume ratio where every portion of the cell is in immediate physical contact with the external medium, allowing simple diffusion to fulfill all metabolic respiration and nutrient uptake.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Two sounds reaching us are heard as separate only if the gap between them is at least 0.1 s. If the speed of sound is 330 m/s, what is the minimum distance of a reflecting wall from which an echo can be heard?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (16.5 m) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). The human ear requires a persistence of hearing interval of at least 0.1 s to perceive an echo distinctly. At sound velocity v = 330 m/s, total round-trip distance 2d = v * t = 330 * 0.1 = 33 m. The minimum distance to the reflecting surface is d = 33 / 2 = 16.5 m.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about energy: 1. The SI unit of energy is the same as the SI unit of work. 2. Energy can be transferred only by doing mechanical work and never as heat. 3. When two objects at different temperatures come in contact, energy flows from the hotter object to the colder object. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (Only 1 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: energy and work share the derived SI unit Joule (J = N*m). Statement 2 is incorrect: energy is readily transferred across thermal boundaries as heat without mechanical displacement. Statement 3 is correct: by the Second Law of Thermodynamics, spontaneous heat conduction proceeds unidirectionally from higher temperature to lower temperature.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The resistivity of copper at 20°C is 1.62 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m. The resistance of a copper wire of length 10 m and cross-sectional area 1.62 × 10⁻⁶ m² at 20°C is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (0.1 Ω) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Resistance R = ρ * L / A = (1.62 * 10^-8 Ω*m * 10 m) / (1.62 * 10^-6 m^2) = (1.62 * 10^-7) / (1.62 * 10^-6) = 0.1 Ω.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In a hilly region, the mountain slopes facing the Sun are heated more rapidly than the valley floor during the day. Which wind is produced as a result?
options: Valley breeze, blowing up the slopes
Mountain breeze, blowing down the slopes
Sea breeze, blowing from the water to the land
Land breeze, blowing from the land to the water
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (Valley breeze, blowing up the slopes) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). During daytime insolation, elevated mountain slopes absorb solar radiation faster than the valley floor, heating contiguous air so it expands and rises, drawing a valley breeze upward along the slopes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Porifera (i) Organ system level (b) Cnidaria (ii) Organ level (c) Platyhelminthes (iii) Cellular level (d) Annelida (iv) Tissue level Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | ((a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Poriferans exhibit cellular-level organisation with minimal coordination (a-iii). Cnidarians exhibit tissue-level organisation with specialized diploblastic layers (b-iv). Platyhelminthes (flatworms) exhibit organ-level organisation (c-ii). Annelids (segmented worms) exhibit organ-system level organisation with closed circulation (d-i).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Respiration in the cells follows C₆H₁₂O₆ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + energy. The number of CO₂ molecules formed when 5 glucose molecules are completely respired is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (30) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). The complete stoichiometric oxidation of glucose is C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O + 38 ATP. One mole of glucose yields 6 moles of CO2. When 5 glucose molecules are respired, they produce 5 * 6 = 30 molecules of CO2.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Compared with an ionic compound such as common salt, camphor (a covalent compound) is expected to have which of the following properties?
options: Higher melting point and good electrical conduction
Lower melting point and no electrical conduction
Higher boiling point and conduction when dissolved
Lower melting point and conduction when molten
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (Lower melting point and no electrical conduction) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Camphor is a non-polar covalent molecular solid held together by weak intermolecular van der Waals forces, giving it a relatively low melting point, volatile sublimation, and zero free ions or electrons to conduct electricity.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Sodium in cold water (i) A thin oxide layer protects it from further corrosion (b) Calcium in cold water (ii) The hydrogen evolved catches fire (c) Aluminium in air (iii) The heat released is not enough for hydrogen to catch fire (d) Silver and gold heated in oxygen (iv) No reaction even at high temperature Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | ((a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iv)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Sodium reacts vigorously with cold water to evolve hydrogen gas, which catches fire with an explosive pop (a-ii). Calcium reacts less violently with water and floats as hydrogen bubbles adhere to it (b-iii). Aluminium forms a self-passivating protective aluminium oxide film upon atmospheric exposure (c-i). Noble metals silver and gold do not react with oxygen even at high temperatures (d-iv).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A box starts moving when it is pushed on a rough floor. Which two forces acting on the box are balanced?
options: Applied force and force of friction
Normal force and force of friction
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (Weight and normal force) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). A box pushed horizontally across a level floor experiences four forces: applied push, friction, downward gravity (weight), and upward normal force. In the vertical direction, the box is in static equilibrium with zero vertical acceleration, meaning normal force balances weight (N = m*g).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Bone (i) Connects bone to bone (b) Cartilage (ii) Connects muscle to bone (c) Tendon (iii) Soft, jelly-like matrix (d) Ligament (iv) Rigid matrix with calcium and phosphorus compounds Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | ((a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Bone consists of an osseous matrix reinforced with calcium phosphate and collagen fibers (a-iv). Cartilage features chondroitin sulphate forming a firm yet pliable resilient matrix (b-iii). Tendons are dense regular connective tissues binding skeletal muscle to bone (c-ii). Ligaments are elastic connective tissues binding bone to bone at joints (d-i).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Many ports on the northwestern coast of Europe stay ice-free in winter even though they lie at high latitudes. Which of the following is the main reason?
options: A cold surface current flowing from the poles
A deep current of dense, highly saline water
The North Atlantic Drift, a warm current
A gyre rotating anticlockwise in the Northern Hemisphere
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (The North Atlantic Drift, a warm current) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Northwestern European coastal ports remain ice-free at high sub-arctic latitudes due to the North Atlantic Drift, a warm ocean current continuation of the Gulf Stream that transports tropical thermal energy northeastward.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the magnetic field produced by a current in a long straight wire: 1. Reversing the direction of the current does not change the direction of the field. 2. At a given point, the magnitude of the field increases as the current through the wire increases. 3. For an unchanged current, the field at a point decreases as its distance from the wire increases. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (Only 2 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is incorrect: reversing current direction inverts the direction of magnetic field lines (determined by Right-Hand Thumb Rule). Statement 2 is correct: magnetic field magnitude B is directly proportional to current I (B ∝ I). Statement 3 is correct: magnetic field strength decays inversely with radial distance r (B ∝ 1/r).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Light travels in a transparent material at a speed of 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s. Taking the speed of light in vacuum as 3 × 10⁸ m/s, the refractive index of the material is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (2) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Refractive index n = speed of light in vacuum (c) / speed of light in medium (v) = (3 * 10^8 m/s) / (1.5 * 10^8 m/s) = 2.0.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A sprinter runs a race by voluntary movements of the legs. Which description fits the fibres of the skeletal muscles that carry out these movements?
options: Long, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate and striated
Short, branched, with a single nucleus and no bands
Long, unbranched, with a single nucleus and no bands
Cuboidal, closely packed, with very little space between them
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (Long, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate and striated) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Skeletal muscle fibers responsible for voluntary limb movement are elongated, unbranched cylindrical syncytial cells containing multiple peripheral nuclei and prominent alternating light/dark transverse striations.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: If the leaves of the plants in a field receive 40,000 kJ of sunlight energy, the energy converted into food energy is about
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (400 kJ) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Terrestrial green plants capture approximately 1% of total incident solar energy falling upon foliage and convert it into photochemical food energy during photosynthesis. 1% of 40,000 kJ = 400 kJ.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II (convex lens): List I List II (a) Object at infinity (i) Real, inverted, same size, at 2F₂ (b) Object at 2F₁ (ii) Virtual, erect, enlarged (c) Object between F₁ and 2F₁ (iii) Real, inverted, enlarged, beyond 2F₂ (d) Object between F₁ and O (iv) Real, inverted, highly diminished, at F₂ Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | ((a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(iii), (d)-(ii)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). For a convex lens: an object at infinity forms a real, inverted, highly diminished point image at focus F2 (a-iv); an object at 2F1 forms a real, inverted, equal-sized image at 2F2 (b-i); an object between F1 and 2F1 forms a real, inverted, magnified image beyond 2F2 (c-iii); an object placed within focal length between F1 and optical center O forms an erect, virtual, magnified image on the same side (d-ii).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about cell division: 1. Meiosis is the most common type of cell division by which cells increase in number. 2. Mitosis is important for normal growth, repair, maintenance and asexual reproduction. 3. Each new cell produced by mitosis gets the same DNA and the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (Only 2 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is incorrect: somatic cell multiplication, tissue renewal, and wound healing occur via mitosis; meiosis is restricted to gametogenesis in gonads. Statement 2 is correct: mitosis drives growth, tissue repair, and asexual propagation. Statement 3 is correct: mitotic cytokinesis produces two genetically identical daughter cells maintaining parental chromosome ploidy.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Echinodermata (i) Notochord present at least once in life (b) Mollusca (ii) Backbone that protects the brain and spinal cord (c) Protochordates (iii) Hard internal skeleton of calcium carbonate (d) Vertebrates (iv) Shell that protects the soft body Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | ((a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Echinoderms possess a spiny endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles (a-iii). Molluscs feature a mantle secreting a protective calcium carbonate shell over a soft visceral mass (b-iv). Protochordates possess a persistent or transient flexible notochord (c-i). Vertebrates replace the embryonic notochord with a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column shielding the spinal cord (d-ii).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Solutions of sodium sulfate and barium chloride are weighed separately and then mixed in a conical flask. A white precipitate appears. Which compound is the precipitate, and what happens to the total mass?
options: Sodium chloride; the total mass increases
Barium sulfate; the total mass decreases
Sodium chloride; the total mass remains unchanged
Barium sulfate; the total mass remains unchanged
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (Barium sulfate; the total mass remains unchanged) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Mixing aqueous solutions of sodium sulphate and barium chloride triggers a double displacement precipitation reaction: Na2SO4(aq) + BaCl2(aq) -> BaSO4(s)↓ + 2NaCl(aq). The white insoluble precipitate is barium sulphate (BaSO4). By the Law of Conservation of Mass, the total mass of the closed reaction system remains unchanged.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A resistor connected across a 12 V source carries a current of 0.6 A. If the potential difference across it is reduced to 9 V, the current through it become
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (0.45) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). According to Ohm's Law (V = I * R), resistance R = V1 / I1 = 12 V / 0.6 A = 20 Ω. When the potential difference is adjusted to 9 V, the new current is I2 = V2 / R = 9 V / 20 Ω = 0.45 A.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Gustatory receptors (i) Detect smell (b) Olfactory receptors (ii) Release of chemicals when the impulse reaches the end of the axon (c) End of the axon (iii) Detect taste (d) Synapse (iv) Gap across which chemicals reach the next neuron Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | ((a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Gustatory receptors located on lingual taste buds detect chemical tastes (a-iii). Olfactory receptors in the nasal epithelium detect airborne odorants (b-i). The axon terminal depolarizes to trigger exocytosis of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft (c-ii). The synapse is the microscopic junction across which neurotransmitters diffuse to activate post-synaptic receptors (d-iv).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about nutrition: 1. Guard cells swell when water flows into them, and the stomatal pore opens. 2. Amoeba takes in food at a specific spot, to which the food is moved by the movement of cilia. 3. Cuscuta, ticks, leeches and tape-worms obtain nutrition from plants or animals without killing them. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (Only 1 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: endosmosis into guard cells generates turgor pressure that curves their elastic walls, opening stomata. Statement 2 is incorrect: Amoeba ingests food at any surface point via pseudopodial phagocytosis (ciliated oral grooves are characteristic of Paramecium). Statement 3 is correct: ectoparasites and endoparasites (Cuscuta, ticks, leeches, tapeworms) derive nourishment without killing their hosts.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Resistors of 4 Ω and 8 Ω are joined in series with a battery. The potential difference across the 8 Ω resistor is 6 V. The potential difference across the battery is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (9 V) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Two resistors (4 Ω and 8 Ω) are connected in series. The current through both components is identical: I = V8 / R8 = 6 V / 8 Ω = 0.75 A. The total equivalent series resistance is R_eq = 4 Ω + 8 Ω = 12 Ω. Total battery voltage V_total = I * R_eq = 0.75 A * 12 Ω = 9 V.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Smooth muscle (i) Long fibre that carries messages away from the cell (b) Cardiac muscle (ii) Receives signals from other neurons (c) Dendrites (iii) Branched cylindrical fibres found only in the heart (d) Axon (iv) Spindle-shaped cells with one nucleus and no striations Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | ((a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Smooth muscle consists of involuntary, spindle-shaped (fusiform) unstriated mononucleate cells found in visceral organs (a-iv). Cardiac muscle features branched, striated, uninucleate cells connected by intercalated discs in the myocardium (b-iii). Dendrites are branched arborizations receiving incoming electro-chemical inputs (c-ii). The axon is a solitary elongated fiber transmitting action potentials away from the soma toward target effectors (d-i).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Assertion (A): Objects seen through the hot air rising above a fire appear to waver. Reason (R): Hot air has a refractive index slightly greater than that of cooler air.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (A is true but R is false) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Assertion (A) is true: hot turbulent air rising above an open flame exhibits fluctuating optical density, causing background light rays to refract erratically and shimmer. Reason (R) is false: thermal expansion lowers the density of heated air, giving it a refractive index slightly less than that of cooler surrounding air.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Assertion (A): In the gold foil experiment, most of the alpha particles passed through the foil without any deflection. Reason (R): Most of the space inside an atom is empty.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R correctly explains A: in Rutherford's gold foil experiment, the overwhelming majority of alpha particles passed straight through with negligible scattering because the vast volume of an atom consists of empty space outside the tiny central nucleus.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: About 2 g of lead nitrate powder is heated in a boiling tube and brown fumes are seen. The products of this decomposition are
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (PbO, NO₂ and O₂) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Thermal decomposition of lead nitrate crystals yields lead(II) oxide, reddish-brown nitrogen dioxide gas, and oxygen gas: 2Pb(NO3)2(s) -> 2PbO(s) + 4NO2(g)↑ + O2(g)↑.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Calcium (i) Reacts with steam to form metal oxide and hydrogen (b) Magnesium (ii) Does not react with water at all (c) Iron (iii) Reacts with cold water and starts floating (d) Copper (iv) Reacts with hot water but not with cold water Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | ((a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Calcium reacts smoothly with cold water to release H2, and floats as bubbles attach to it (a-iii). Magnesium reacts with hot boiling water or steam to form Mg(OH)2 and H2 (b-iv). Iron reacts only with steam at red heat to form magnetic oxide Fe3O4 and H2 (c-i). Copper lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series and does not react with water or steam at any temperature (d-ii).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about human reproduction: 1. The mother always contributes an X chromosome to the baby. 2. A child is female if the father contributes a Y chromosome. 3. From about the ninth week of pregnancy, the developing embryo is called a foetus. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | (Only 1 and 3) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: human females are homogametic (XX) and always donate an X chromosome in ova. Statement 2 is incorrect: an ovum fertilized by a Y-bearing sperm produces a male infant (XY); fertilization by an X-bearing sperm produces a female (XX). Statement 3 is correct: human embryonic organogenesis is established by 8 weeks, after which the developing conceptus is termed a fetus.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Hydrogen is combustible and oxygen supports combustion. What is true of water, the compound formed when they combine?
options: It neither burns nor helps in burning, and it extinguishes fire
It is a gas with properties between those of hydrogen and oxygen
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option B | (It neither burns nor helps in burning, and it extinguishes fire) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Water (H2O) is a distinct chemical compound synthesized from combustible hydrogen and combustion-supporting oxygen. The chemical properties of a compound differ fundamentally from its constituent elements: liquid water neither burns nor supports combustion, functioning as a premier fire extinguisher.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about contraception: 1. A condom works as a mechanical barrier so that sperm does not reach the egg. 2. Oral contraceptive pills change the hormonal balance of the body so that eggs are not released. 3. A copper-T placed in the uterus also protects a woman from sexually transmitted diseases. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (Only 1 and 2) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: latex condoms provide a physical barrier preventing semen from entering the female reproductive tract. Statement 2 is correct: combined oral contraceptive pills release synthetic estrogen/progesterone to suppress pituitary gonadotropins (FSH/LH), preventing ovulation. Statement 3 is incorrect: copper-T intrauterine devices prevent blastocyst fertilization and implantation, but provide no prophylactic protection against sexually transmitted infections (STIs).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a supporting (simple permanent) tissue of plants?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option D | (Phloem) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma are simple permanent plant tissues composed of a single cell type performing support and storage. Phloem is a complex permanent vascular tissue comprising sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibres.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Consider the following statements about carbon in the ocean: 1. Ocean water absorbs atmospheric CO₂ to form carbonate and bicarbonate ions. 2. Phytoplankton use carbonate and bicarbonate ions for photosynthesis. 3. CO₂ moves only from the atmosphere into the ocean and never in the opposite direction. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A | (Only 1 and 2) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). Statement 1 is correct: atmospheric CO2 dissolves into ocean surface waters, reacting with H2O to form carbonic acid, bicarbonate (HCO3-), and carbonate (CO3^2-) ions. Statement 2 is correct: marine phytoplankton fix dissolved inorganic carbon during aquatic photosynthesis. Statement 3 is incorrect: oceanic CO2 flux is a bidirectional dynamic equilibrium with outgassing occurring in warm tropical waters.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Match List I with List II: List I List II (a) Electric bulb (i) Chemical energy to mechanical energy (b) Electric water heater (ii) Mechanical energy to sound energy (c) Muscles using food (iii) Electrical energy to light energy (d) Ringing bell (iv) Electrical energy to thermal energy Select the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option C | ((a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii)) | Exam: RRB Science Top 300 Series (Group D / ALP / Tech / JE). An incandescent bulb converts electrical energy into light energy and waste heat (a-iii). An electric water heater uses resistive Joule heating to convert electrical energy into thermal energy (b-iv). Skeletal muscles hydrolyze ATP to transform chemical energy into mechanical muscular contraction (c-i).
